_changes: PARKED for Encounter's brawl (docs/director/brawl-plan.md), built on the live file and still the live file plus what is listed here. From the first version: `beat` (the beat point by path), on every `pieces` row a `path`, with `sends` on the heavies, and two pools for each fighter (brawl.flurry, brawl.skill). For three strengths (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md, slice C2a): `brawl` now maps each press of X, Y and B to a pool; four more pools for each fighter (brawl.medium, brawl.medium.held, brawl.heavy, and brawl.lift re-read as the rising mediums); the `burst` block with three pools (burst.fast, burst.mid, burst.slow) and a sample for each lean; the `fallback` block; for slice C2t the `launcher` block with its pool (brawl.launcher) and the `reach` block; and pieces rows for the strikes of Animation's later packs (rival4, protag7) that the new pools name, with those packs named in `_status`; one path re-read from Animation (the crossed-arm ram travels a line). Gone: brawl.break and the ender, with their rules. Nothing that is live is changed. Drop _target and _changes when it lands
_about: PARKED: ready to become data/combat/recipes.json as it stands (drop _target), but not moved. The pieces each of Game Design's recipes calls (docs/design/agency-pass.md section 2), per fighter. Fighter keys are the neutral working ids (protagonist, rival) until Orb names the pair. The rules and numbers quoted are Game Design's; the director's own numbers (the window, the flow's thresholds, the multipliers) belong in Encounter's data/director/alchemy.json. Checked against HEAD 45a95b9: every posed id is a strike of a wave manifest, and every blur step fills for both fighters.

_status.live: plays in live matches today. Nothing in these pools does yet: KAI and VORR still draw on the placeholder key sets, and go-live step 1 is a flag, off
_status.posed: posed in one of Animation's packs and parked: it plays when its fighter lands (wave 1, rival2 and rival4 for the rival; protag1, protag6 and protag7 for the Protagonist). The director may draw on posed and live pieces alike
_status.waiting: not posed yet: the director skips it

base._plays: the plain blur, mashed off the beat: the string's pattern with loose contact; each strike at the mashed share of a light (data/director/launch.json blur.strikeMul); no flow, because the presses are off the beat
base._endsIn: knock-back, the weak one: blur.enderDist of the tier's distance and setup.weight.blurPlain of a set-up (launch.json); never a launch

timed._from: the fourth press in a row that is evenly spaced and within 2 ticks of one of the blur's blows landing (agency-pass.md section 20)
timed.plays: the perfect blur, from that press on: the same pattern locks in and every strike lands clean, at a light's full damage; each on-beat press adds 1 to flow
timed.endsIn: knock-back, the full one: the pattern's own closing blow, the tier's full distance and a full set-up; never a launch
timed._look: full contact on every strike, a thin outline of his aura, and a rising accent in the sound for each blow (VFX and Audio)

timed.plays: a guard-breaking blow; unguarded it earns a launch

flow.from3: launch: power.last, by the stick through sends
flow.at5: a showcase ender when its gates pass

direction.away: a retreat entry, a heavy from combo.accent at knock-back force, blasts

patternGates._about: When a pattern may be drawn, read at the string's first blow. A pattern with no row is always open. stick: the stick's direction at that press; with the stick toward, the draw is among the patterns gated to toward, and without it those are closed. ground: both fighters are on the ground. fighters: only these fighters' strings draw it

patternRule: every blur string draws one open pattern, with its cadence, at its first blow (patternGates). Each light of the string takes the next step, filled from the fighter's blur lights with that limb and target (pieces), no key strike twice in a string; a string that runs past the fifth step starts the pattern again. The pattern's own closing blow is drawn from the ender pool and lands where the string's last light landed, when a piece of that pool does; otherwise any piece of it. A pattern carries no ticks: the gap between blows is the string's cadence, the director's number

beat._about: The beat point of a light or a skill strike: ticks after its contact at which the next press is on the beat (Game Design: 24 by default, 20 to 28 by the piece). By the piece's path. default serves a piece with no path

brawl._about: Which pool each press in the martial arts stance draws on, for three strengths (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 8): X a light, Y a medium, B a heavy. One press is one attack: the pool is the button's, and the press changes only how it is thrown. X: light (tapped), lightToward (tapped with the stick toward the rival), flurry (mashed), skill (on the beat), juggle; a held X is the `burst` block. Y: medium (tapped, mashed and on the beat) is the mediums that read on a 12-tick wind-up; mediumHeld (a held Y, slice C2b) is every medium, the ones that need a long wind-up included. B: heavy (tapped, mashed and on the beat) and heavyHeld (slice C2b). No piece of the heavy tier is posed, so brawl.heavy holds STAND-INS: his posed pieces that only read on a long wind-up, played on B's. The tier's own pieces (docs/combat/pending/movegen) replace them as they are drawn. lift is the pair X+Y (slice C6a). The pools for Y and B come from the generated movesets, so they keep to each fighter's identity: the rival's have no palm and no blade hand. When a pool has nothing it may throw, `fallback` says what is thrown. launcher is a tap of B on a staggered rival (section 3 of the design page): see the `launcher` block. With RB held in reach, X and Y are the energy pieces of the `reach` block, which are not strikes and have no pool

burst._about: A held X: eight lights that slow on a curve (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 3). The first is the light the press threw. Each later blow comes from the pool of the gap before it: fast for a gap of 5 ticks or fewer (hands only, on a path with no raise and no turn), mid for 6 to 8 (an elbow or a knee fits), slow for 9 or more (any light). The gaps are Game Design's and live in the director's data; slots names their classes in order. rules are what keep a 4-tick gap from reading as a stutter, judged on the pieces table (limb, path, target) together with Legal's string rules. Every light a tap can throw can open a whole burst under them (gen_moveset.py --check tests it). close is the path each fighter's eighth blow takes when the rules leave him one. samples are one whole burst for each lean of the stick, for Animation's study and for the director to play as they are

rules.rule: never the same limb on the same path twice running: the same blow thrown again 4 ticks later is a stutter
never the same place twice running: the sparks would stack on one point
no more than two blows running on one path: three straights read as one blow played three times
no piece twice in one burst

fallback._about: What a press throws when its pool has nothing it may throw. No press is silent (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 8). A piece may be thrown when it is not one of his last two pieces (the director's own rule, for variety) and breaks none of Legal's string rules, which count the whole string whatever buttons made it (docs/legal/movegen-banned.json s01, s02, s04, s05, f02). The steps are tried in order. Legal's rules are never dropped

steps.what: a piece of the press's pool, under both rules
one of his last two pieces again, the older first, when Legal's rules allow it. Only the director's variety rule gives way
a piece of the pool one strength down, thrown on this button's wind-up and at this button's worth: brawl.medium for a heavy, combo.link for a medium

heavyOnStandIns._about: Why this block exists today: B runs on a handful of stand-ins. How often each step is reached, over every two blows of his three pools that Legal's rules allow (all) and over two stand-ins running, which is a mashed B (mashedB). Counted on the pieces table. runsDry lists every mashed B that leaves no stand-in to throw; it is empty for both fighters, since the Protagonist's spinning heel was taken out of his stand-ins for that (with it, three strings ran dry, and repeating was not allowed either). The steps above stay as the net. This block goes when the heavy tier's ten are posed, which never run dry (after any two blows at least 4 of the rival's and 5 of the Protagonist's may follow)

launcher._about: A tap of B on a staggered rival: it always lands and launches (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 3, slice C2t). The stick nudges the launch and the director stages it; this is only the blow that starts it, picked by where it sends. aim: the stick's lean to the send wanted. noStick: with no stick the launch planner's pick decides the send, and the piece is one that sends that way. bySend: the pool's pieces by where each sends (its path). Until the heavy tier is posed these are STAND-INS: first his heavy stand-ins that read on half the wind-up (a spin or a leap does not), then his posed mediums that land on the trunk or the head, which were the launching blows before the three strengths. A medium that one of his own never rows would bar as a heavy is left out (the Protagonist never brings one down on a head). The tier's own launchers replace them: every send has at least one (docs/combat/pending/movegen/review-sheet.md)

reach._about: Energy in reach (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 5b, slice C2t): with RB held in a brawl, X is the point-blank bolt and Y the blast. pieces are the generated moves (docs/combat/pending/movegen): an energy hand, how it is let go, the place it is set on, and the path it has in a string (a thrust is a line, a flick an outward arc, a sweep an inward arc). set is the posed press or shot it is played on, when there is one. They count as blows in Legal's string rules. rule: Legal's e06 counts a piece by its hand and release, so a mash never throws the same hand and release twice running; the four bolts differ in one or the other, and one may always follow. run: Legal's e09 for a mashed run, as numbers the director can order by, with the arm (lead or free) for each bolt. runs: two sample runs of twelve a fighter

run._about: A mashed run of point-blank bolts, ordered by Legal's e09 so that it reads as varied on screen and not only in data. An arm is lead or free: which arm throws a bolt is chosen for each throw, and Animation mirrors the piece. samePlacePathArm: never the same arm, path and place twice running. pathsIn: at least so many different paths in any so many bolts running. freeArm: the free arm takes a bolt now and then, never two in three (so never a left-right pump), at least one in six, and never on a regular count (two gaps running between its bolts are never equal). notPeriodic: the order of the pieces never repeats on a fixed count of 3 or 4. A run also keeps what every string keeps: never one of his last two pieces, e06, and the string rules. Each hand lands on the chest or the gut, below the collar line; the heads keep a hand's width apart (Animation)
run._proof: a run of this many bolts must exist for each fighter (three seconds of mashing, the length Legal will watch): --check tries to make one

pieces._about: Each pool strike's striking limb and the socket it lands on, one row per strike id, shared by both fighters (each fighter's own key set plays it). The director fills a blur pattern's steps from these, and Tools checks them against Animation's manifests. limb: hand, foot, elbow, knee, shoulder, head or own. target: a socket of data/anim/sockets.json. path: the angle the limb travels (line, arc_in, arc_out, rise, drop, spin); it gives the piece its beat point (beat). sends, on a heavy: where it sends the rival when it ends a string (across, up, down, turned), for the stick's aim

lastPress._endings: the looks are parked in templates.brawl.json. The knock-back itself is live: data/director/launch.json knockBack and the director's knockBack op, whose event kinds are slideShort, slideLong, bump and drift

showcase._about: The flow's top ending (flow.at5): a showcase ender replaces the plain ender when a row's gates pass; with no row open, the launch keeps its panel and its extra wear on the plain ender. A row is open when its strike is the string's ender, the launch goes its way (sends) and, where given, there is clearAboveBh of open air above the pair. Rows are per fighter; waiting rows are skipped (their held moments are wave 7's sketches)
